epic.title: Migration from React to Angular using AI (internship)

fields.currentSituation: The frontend is implemented in React and the migration work needs a reviewable hierarchy and evidence-driven delivery flow.
fields.desiredOutcome: Migrate bounded frontend features to Angular with reusable AI-assisted analysis, implementation and verification evidence.
fields.whyMatters: The internship must prove a safe migration approach while keeping stakeholders informed about scope, progress and risk.
successCriteria: Each Feature and User Story has a clear bounded outcome.
Progress is derived from completed stakeholder-visible Tasks.
Verified migration evidence supports the decision for each next slice.
fields.richReleaseNotes: First bounded slice of the Map Making Page migration (the Detail Drawer LineForm Length/Angle/Fence offset fields) is implemented locally and validated; independent verification remains, and the baseline/implementation Targetprocess items still need to be applied.

epic.structureComment:
EPIC - Migration from React to Angular using AI (internship)
|
+-- Feature - Migrate Map Making Page
    |
    +-- User Story - Migrate Detail Drawer (Length, Angle, Fence offset, Done)

fields.currentSituation: The map-making experience, including the Detail Drawer, is implemented entirely in React with direct drawlib integrations.
fields.desiredOutcome: Migrate bounded map-making slices to Angular while preserving observable behavior, starting with the LineForm Length/Angle/Fence offset editing flow.
fields.whyMatters: A bounded migration reduces integration risk and produces reusable migration evidence for the remaining Detail Drawer forms.
successCriteria: The approved Detail Drawer LineForm slice preserves its agreed scenarios.
React retains the drawer shell, shared inputs/radio components and canvas ownership during this slice.
fields.richReleaseNotes: Detail Drawer LineForm slice (Length, Angle, Fence offset selector and distance) implemented in Angular behind the approved React boundary; targeted test, typecheck and build all pass. Independent verification remains, and the Targetprocess items for this slice still need to be applied.

fields.userValue: As a map editor, I want to edit Length, Angle and, where available, Fence offset of the line I have selected or am drawing, and close with Done, so the map updates without losing existing behavior.
fields.currentBehavior: Angular now owns the Length, Angle and Fence offset (selector plus distance value) fields, mounted inside the retained React LineForm.tsx via createApplication()/createComponent(); LineForm.tsx keeps owning the Selected Line label, LineRiskCard, Detectable section, Coordinates/Distances, Done button and delete button.
fields.desiredBehavior: The same scenarios must pass independent verification and the required manual Route Assistant desktop validation before the slice counts as done.
acceptanceCriteria: The drawer shows the selected line's Length and Angle, and its Fence offset when the active robot has the FeedPush capability.
Valid edits update the SVG line and preserve undo/redo exactly as today, including the key-press-gated history rule for Length and Angle.
An empty, non-numeric, zero-length or unchanged value is silently ignored, matching today's guards.
Fence offset controls are fully absent when the active robot lacks the FeedPush capability.
Closing with the retained Done button and reopening does not retain stale state or duplicate listeners.
attentionPoints: Local validation (targeted test, typecheck, build) is not proof of independent verification.
Validate the required manual scenario in the Route Assistant desktop host before proposing Done.
The baseline and implementation Targetprocess items still need to be applied manually; this handoff does not assume they were.
Do not edit FocusNumberInput.tsx or the RadioButton family; they remain untouched and are reused only via shared design tokens and copied icon SVG data in the Angular slice.
fields.attachmentInformation: Attach the validated migration-result.json reference; do not attach source copies.
fields.richReleaseNotes: Length, Angle and Fence offset (selector + distance) are implemented in Angular and validated locally (targeted test, typecheck, build all pass); independent verification and the required manual host validation remain before this slice is done.

tasks.title: Establish Detail Drawer LineForm behavior baseline

Acceptance scenarios, characterization hypotheses and decisions are visible.

tasks.title: Implement the bounded Angular Length/Angle/Fence offset fields
tasks.description: Add the missing React characterization tests and implement the approved Angular slice with scoped checkpoints, inside the write allowlist only.
doneWhen: The Angular slice and its matching tests pass.
Every product checkpoint stays inside scope.allowedWritePaths.
evidence: Added FocusNumberInput.characterization.test.tsx, proving the 300ms debounce and keyboard-shortcut suspension against the retained React component before implementing the Angular fields.

Implemented src/features/floorPlanCreator/detailDrawer/lineForm/angular/ (line-fields.component.ts, mount-line-fields.ts, AngularLineFieldsHost.tsx, line-fields.types.ts) and wired it into LineForm.tsx.

Added LineForm.angular-line-fields.test.tsx, rendering the real LineForm parent tree and proving valid-length-edit, fence-offset-selection-when-capable, fence-offset-hidden-when-incapable and restore-invalid-length end to end.
npm run test -- run .../LineForm.functions.test.ts (24 tests), npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build all passed.
checkpointPolicy.mode is 'disabled' in the Flow Contract, so no local commit was created; all changes remain as uncommitted worktree changes inside scope.allowedWritePaths.

tasks.description: Independently verify all contract scenarios and the required manual host scenario before proposing Done.

Ran the declared targeted test, typecheck and build; all passed.
